items.defect: D33 depends on a verifier capability that nothing creates. It says, "`verify-refs.mjs` parses every `path:line` and `path` reference out of the phase specs and this file, and asserts each path exists and each cited line contains the quoted token." The checked-in verifier does not parse inline `path:line` references at all, and no phase requires changing that script.
items.requiredFix: Add the verifier itself and a verifier test to the spec-tooling scope. Parse every inline `path:line` citation from all five required Markdown files, verify the cited line semantically against an adjacent quoted token, and add a negative fixture proving an uncatalogued stale citation makes the command fail.
items.evidence: `.claude/work/prompt-lanes/spec-v2/verify-refs.mjs:27` defines `PATH_RE` for backticked paths without `:line`; lines 34-45 only check those paths. Lines 47-85 validate hand-authored `claims*.json` entries, not every citation in the Markdown. Therefore A40/A34/A29 can exit 0 while an uncatalogued inline citation is stale.

items.defect: A7 and A8 depend on an archive that A6 explicitly prevents from being created. A6 begins, "With `output.archive: false`", while A7 says, "Replacing week 1's archive snapshot text ... before the A6 week-2 build" and A8 says, "Deleting week 1's archive directory before the A6 week-2 build". No requirement in that scenario creates the snapshot or directory to replace or delete.

items.defect: Phase 4 consumes authored-versus-engine provenance that Phase 3 never mints. R3 requires, "A current authored row wins" but later says, "a selected prior nonterminal entry wins over ... a nonterminal current engine row". The final D34 row schema has no provenance field, and Phase 4 R1 accepts only those final rows, so its pure transition cannot distinguish the two precedence branches.
items.requiredFix: Amend D34/D47 and Phase 3 to mint explicit local-only provenance, such as `sourceKind: 'authored' | 'engine'`, or pass two separately typed candidate collections into the Phase 4 transition. Require stripping that provenance before any renderer or archive snapshot and test both same-ref branches through the actual cross-phase interface.
items.evidence: `phase-2.md:392-409` gives the final forward shape as id, text, origin, receipt, ref, and optional repo/closedBy. `phase-3.md:83-102` constructs and merges authored and engine candidates but defines no retained provenance value in the final private row. `phase-4.md:62-73` accepts those rows, while `phase-4.md:93-99` requires different results based on provenance. Origin cannot substitute: authored rows may legitimately copy either handoff origin.

items.defect: Phase 3 consumes `ideasTruncatedAtTurn` as a truncation signal, but Phase 1 cannot mint a distinct signal when the first dropped idea is pre-boundary. Phase 1 requires pre-boundary ideas to have `turn: null` and also uses `ideasTruncatedAtTurn: number | null`, with `null` already meaning no truncation. A session-level cap can therefore drop a pre-boundary idea while emitting the same turn value as the no-drop state.
items.requiredFix: Define truncation presence as `ideasDropped > 0` in D39/D44 and Phase 3, using `ideasTruncatedAtTurn` only as optional location context. Add a pre-boundary session-cap acceptance case that reports the exact dropped count even though the first dropped idea has no numeric turn.
items.evidence: `decisions.md:605-610` and `phase-1.md:101-104` require pre-boundary ideas to use null turns. `phase-1.md:96-101` records the first dropped idea in a number-or-null `ideasTruncatedAtTurn`. `phase-3.md:79-80` calls that field "the D39 truncation signal", while `phase-3.md:135` relies on it for the diagnostic. D44's `ideasDropped` count exists, but the Phase 3 signal rule does not use `ideasDropped > 0`.

items.defect: The no-input corpus rule is stated incompatibly in Phase 3 and Phase 4. Phase 3 says build must use the shared operation to discover engine rows even when both authored arrays are absent; Phase 4 A2 says that with no current D34 rows and no index, "no ... corpus reader is called." The absence of current engine rows cannot be known without the Phase 3 scan, so Phase 4's zero-call rule disables D6 engine discovery.
items.requiredFix: Change Phase 4 R1/A2 to require no additional corpus scan beyond Phase 3's one mandatory engine-presence derivation. It may skip the carry reader and index writer, but it must reuse the already-derived empty corpus result.
items.evidence: `phase-3.md:139-146` says engine presence is determined independently of authored keys, and A2 at `phase-3.md:211-213` requires exactly one shared-corpus call for `undefined`, `null`, and `[]`. `phase-4.md:69-72` says to skip the lane corpus in the empty result, and A2 at `phase-4.md:212-214` requires no corpus reader call. D6 at `decisions.md:190-197` makes engine-only handoff rows mandatory.

items.defect: Carry re-gating can be bypassed because source-repo provenance is optional and author-controlled. Phase 2 says "`repo` ... [is] optional"; Phase 3 lets the resolved source override only origin and receipt; Phase 4 preserves an "optional `repo`" and tests a role change only when it happens to be present. A row may therefore be persisted without its real source repo, or with a different featured label, and later survive when the source repo becomes `display`.
items.requiredFix: Require Phase 3 to derive `repo` from the resolved session or handoff for every private forward row, reject any conflicting authored repo value, persist the derived label in every carry entry, and make the Phase 4 display-role gate fail closed when required provenance is absent.

A15 at `phase-4.md:265-269` covers only a populated optional field, not omission or falsification.

R2 changes existing legacy steering, redirect, assistant-thinking, and assistant-text bytes from truncate-then-redact to redact-then-truncate even when none of the new lane inputs is present. R1 says to update AGENTS with a named exception, but AGENTS calls byte additivity an invariant that "must not break."

Preserve legacy field bytes in the prompt-lanes revision and apply redaction-first only to new fields, or split the legacy privacy migration into a separately authorized invariant change with its own version/migration contract before this phase begins.

The live adapter truncates first at `lib/claude-adapter.mjs:311-314` and redacts legacy values later at `lib/claude-adapter.mjs:500-518`, so R2 necessarily changes existing local-state bytes for boundary cases; A6 itself pins such a change.

That violates AGENTS invariant 6's absent-input byte identity, and unlike the Phase 1 local-state reorder it is not even named as an exception.

(<mode>, <N> item(s), <bytes> bytes).` `phase-2.md:342-347` unconditionally inserts two zero-count clauses from Phase 2 onward. The lane-absent acceptance criteria compare artifacts, not stdout, so this invariant break is untested.

items.defect: The `closedBy` rule permits an unsupported outcome. It explicitly says, "`build` verifies that the cited reversal exists, not that it is semantically related", yet Phase 3 turns that weak check into the disposition `ruled out` for the authored idea. The output therefore asserts that one idea was ruled out when the log may contain only an unrelated reversal.
items.requiredFix: Remove `closedBy` as `ruled out` evidence unless the source format carries an explicit machine-verifiable relation to the same ref. Until such a relation is minted, only a row directly resolved to the cited reversal ref may derive `ruled out`; all other authored rows must stay `not started`.
items.evidence: `phase-2.md:369-375` defines the weak `closedBy` verification; `phase-3.md:105-120` and A17 at lines 280-282 derive `ruled out` from it. `AGENTS.md:44-45` requires under-claiming and says, "Never assert a motive, cause, or outcome the log does not contain." Mere co-location in a handoff does not establish the relationship the disposition claims.

items.defect: D5 treats an 8-hex FNV-1a hash as collision-free identity: "Collisions across kinds are prevented by `kind` being in the canonical string." Including kind prevents identical canonical strings across kinds, but a 32-bit hash still collides. D39 then uses the same 8-hex construction as the sole grouping key for the `repeated without correction` honesty claim. No decision requires detecting collisions before ref joins or shape grouping.
items.requiredFix: Keep the compact hash only as a display/local lookup token if desired, but retain the canonical identity tuple and normalized six-word shape internally. Detect any same-hash/different-canonical collision before a join or grade and abort/drop loudly; add the concrete collision pairs as acceptance fixtures.
items.evidence: The actual FNV-1a implementation is 32-bit at `lib/handoffs.mjs:39-46`. Applying that exact algorithm gives a cross-kind ref collision: `turn|6666018e|80888` and `handoff-reversal|dd8b4025|143711` both hash to `40adc0a2`. It also gives a shape collision between `mvwovw mdhcrz oxtqfa nbudte ufxhqs frynja` and `crnqqs biirkm oqhrsx hytals fnldcq jtyhun`, both `6d566ca3`. D5's claim is at `decisions.md:159-160`; D39/D36 group solely by the 8-hex shape key at `decisions.md:813-820` and `decisions.md:756-762`.
